title: Accurate and Scalable Estimation of Epistemic Uncertainty for Graph Neural Networks

en.text: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly being handed high-stakes jobs: predicting molecular properties, screening materials, flagging anomalies. These settings share an uncomfortable feature: the data a model sees at test time almost never matches what it trained on. Graphs grow larger, their structure drifts, and the relationships between labels and attributes shift. In those moments we care about more than whether the model is right; we care about whether its confidence is right. Downstream safety metrics, from calibration error to out-of-distribution (OOD) rejection to generalization-gap estimation, all sit on top of that confidence indicator, which usually comes from a softmax probability or an entropy score.

The computer vision community has known for years that confidence quality decays under distribution shift. For graph neural networks, how and why confidence degrades has been studied far less. This paper (ICLR 2024) fills that gap systematically, and then offers a direct fix.

A natural first instinct is to reach for a more expressive architecture and assume better calibration comes along for free. Through a controlled experiment, the authors show it does not. Figure 1 makes the counterintuitive result hard to miss.

en.caption: Figure 1. Calibration under structural distortion shift. Models are trained on standard super-pixel MNIST and then evaluated on k-nearest-neighbor graphs built from rotated MNIST images, using the rotation angle to dial the structural distortion from mild to severe. The top row is accuracy (higher is better); the bottom row is expected calibration error, ECE (lower is better). As the shift grows, the accuracy drop is expected, but ECE deteriorates sharply too, and switching to a graph transformer (GPS), adding positional encodings (LPE), or making the network deeper and wider does not rescue it. Only the proposed G-∆UQ (blue) drives ECE down substantially without materially sacrificing accuracy.

en.text: In other words, piling on expressivity is not the cure for miscalibration, and scaling depth or width can even make it worse. What is actually needed is to model epistemic uncertainty explicitly. That is where the paper begins.
Paper and code
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10976
Code: https://github.com/pujacomputes/gduq
Project page: https://pujacomputes.github.io/gduq/
What the paper contributes

The contribution comes in three escalating steps. First, a controlled case study establishing that improving a GNN's expressivity does not fix confidence calibration under distribution shift. Second, G-∆UQ, a single-model uncertainty method that ports the stochastic centering (anchoring) framework to graph data and, crucially, supports partial stochasticity (making only part of the network stochastic), including a variant that reuses a pretrained backbone as-is. Third, an extensive evaluation across three types of distribution shift and three safety-critical tasks.

The single-model point is worth dwelling on. Unlike Deep Ensembles, which train many models and average them, G-∆UQ needs just one model to produce both a prediction and an estimate of its uncertainty.
How G-∆UQ works

Start with the method at a glance. The core idea is anchoring: instead of feeding the model the raw input, you first draw a random anchor c from the training distribution and rewrite the input as a relative representation: subtract the anchor, then concatenate it back, i.e. [X − c ‖ c]. Each iteration uses a different anchor, so the model behaves as if it were sampling from a family of hypotheses. Run the same sample through K different anchors, and the variance of those predictions captures epistemic uncertainty.

en.caption: Figure 2. Overview of G-∆UQ. The authors propose three stochastic centering variants that inject increasing-to-decreasing amounts of stochasticity into the GNN: anchoring on the node features (Node Feature), at an intermediate message-passing layer (Int. MPNN), or after the READOUT (Readout). Blue marks the stochastic part, red the static part. The READOUT variant makes only the post-readout head stochastic, so it can wrap a pretrained backbone directly. On the right is anchored inference: average over K anchors for the prediction μ, use the standard deviation σ across anchors as the uncertainty, and report the calibrated prediction μ_calib = μ(1 − σ).

en.text: Why anchor in feature space rather than on the graph structure itself? Subtracting an "anchor graph" from an adjacency matrix would invent edges that do not exist and corrupt the graph's meaning. So the authors anchor in node-feature or hidden-representation space instead. The three variants correspond to injecting the anchor early, in the middle, or late; the later the injection, the smaller and lighter the stochastic part. The variant that freezes a pretrained backbone and trains only an anchored classifier head adds uncertainty to an existing model at almost no cost. That is what partial stochasticity buys you in practice.
Results across three kinds of shift

The evaluation is deliberately broad. Structural distortion uses the rotated super-pixel MNIST benchmark from Figure 1. Size shift uses four graph-classification datasets (D&D, NCI1, NCI109, PROTEINS) with GCN, GIN, and PNA backbones. Concept and covariate shift use the GOOD benchmark suite (GOODCMNIST-color, GOODMotif-basis, GOODMotif-size, GOODSST2-length). The baselines are Vanilla, Deep Ensembles (DEns), temperature scaling (Temp), and Monte Carlo Dropout (MCD). Start with size shift.

en.caption: Figure 4. Predictive uncertainty under size distribution shift. Each pair compares G-∆UQ (blue) against a no-anchoring baseline (Base, gray), with accuracy on top (higher is better) and ECE on the bottom (lower is better). Across D&D, NCI1, NCI109, and PROTEINS and across the GCN, GIN, and PNA backbones, stochastic centering almost always lowers calibration error while maintaining or improving accuracy.

en.text: For concept and covariate shift, the authors line G-∆UQ up directly against the other single-model UQ methods.

en.caption: Figure 5. Predictive uncertainty under concept and covariate shift. Spanning the four GOOD datasets, each split into concept and covariate shift, the four rows are in-distribution accuracy (ID Acc), out-of-distribution accuracy (OOD Acc), in-distribution calibration (ID Cal L2), and out-of-distribution calibration (OOD Cal L2). Stochastic anchoring keeps ID and OOD accuracy competitive while improving calibration, and the advantage is clearest against the other single-model UQ methods.

en.text: One line summarizes all three figures: whether the shift comes from structure, size, or concept and covariate, G-∆UQ delivers more trustworthy confidence than the other single-model methods, with accuracy essentially untouched.
What better confidence actually buys you

Calibration is only a means. The real payoff is whether those calibrated confidence estimates, when fed into downstream safety tasks, produce better results. The authors examine two: generalization-gap prediction and out-of-distribution detection.

en.caption: Figure 6. Generalization-gap prediction. Confidence scores from each method are used to predict the generalization error, reported as mean absolute error, MAE (lower is better), with in-distribution on top and out-of-distribution on the bottom. No single method dominates, but stochastic anchoring is highly competitive and yields among the lowest MAE of the single-model UQ estimators; the pretrained G-∆UQ variant is especially effective, even outperforming the end-to-end version.

en.text: Generalization-gap prediction, estimating how much a model will degrade without peeking at test labels, is a task that has barely been explored for graphs. That the pretrained variant beats the end-to-end one here is a practical signal: you do not have to retrain from scratch to get good uncertainty.

en.caption: Figure 7. OOD detection. AUROC for detecting out-of-distribution samples (higher is better). Under concept shift, the G-∆UQ variants are competitive with all baselines, including Deep Ensembles. Under covariate shift, with the sole exception of GOODMotif-basis, pretrained G-∆UQ delivers significant gains over every baseline, including end-to-end G-∆UQ.

en.text: Taken together, the two downstream tasks reveal a recurring pattern: under covariate shift, the hardest case, pretrained G-∆UQ is frequently the strongest of the lot. The cheapest way to use the method, freezing the backbone and training only the head, is often also the best.
A key ablation: where to anchor

If anchoring can go early, middle, or late, does the choice matter? The authors ablate it on D&D, the dataset with the most severe size shift. Anchoring after the READOUT (the last layer) makes both accuracy and calibration improve markedly as the network deepens, while earlier-layer anchoring converges less cleanly. That yields a practical recommendation: when a model is expected to face size shift, anchor at the last layer. A neural tangent kernel (NTK) analysis further confirms that applying constant shifts at intermediate layers genuinely changes the function the GNN represents, rather than acting as a trivial reparameterization that cancels out.
Takeaway and boundaries

The core message is plain: do not expect a larger, more expressive graph neural network to hand you trustworthy confidence: under distribution shift, it will not. The move that works is to carry the principle of stochastic anchoring over to graphs. G-∆UQ is a flexible, scalable, single-model framework that produces reliable, well-calibrated uncertainty across structural, size, concept, and covariate shifts, and across the three safety tasks of calibration, generalization-gap prediction, and OOD detection.

And its pretrained variant makes all of that nearly free to bolt onto a model you have already trained. The honest boundary: these conclusions rest on the paper's specific datasets, backbones, and shift setups, and the best anchoring layer depends on the task (last-layer is recommended for size shift). Carrying the method to a new setting still deserves the same kind of validation the authors ran here.

zh.text: 图神经网络（Graph Neural Network, GNN）正在被越来越多地放到高风险场景里：分子性质预测、材料筛选、异常检测。这些场景有一个共同点——真正的测试数据几乎不可能和训练时长得一模一样。图的规模会变、结构会变、类别与属性的关联也会变。这时候我们通常不只看模型「答得对不对」，还要看它给出的置信度（confidence indicator，通常来自 softmax 概率或熵）「可不可信」，因为校准误差、分布外（OOD）拒识、泛化间隙估计这些安全指标，全都建立在这个置信度之上。
计算机视觉领域早就知道：一旦发生分布偏移，模型的置信度质量就会明显变差。但对图神经网络来说，置信度在分布偏移下如何、以及为什么会退化，研究得要少得多。本文（ICLR 2024）系统地补上了这一课，并给出了一个直接的解决方案。
一个很自然的想法是：换更强、更有表达力的架构，校准问题是不是就能顺带解决？作者用一个受控实验给出的答案是——不能。图 1 把这个反直觉的结论摆得很清楚。

zh.caption: 图 1　结构失真分布偏移下的校准表现。作者在标准 super-pixel MNIST 上训练模型，再把它放到由「先旋转、再构图」得到的 k-近邻图上评测，用旋转角度模拟由弱到强的结构失真。上排是准确率（越高越好），下排是期望校准误差 ECE（越低越好）。随着偏移加剧，准确率下降在意料之中，但 ECE 也急剧变差——而且换成图 transformer（GPS）、加位置编码（LPE）、加深加宽网络，都救不回来。只有本文提出的 G-∆UQ（蓝色）在几乎不牺牲准确率的前提下，把 ECE 大幅压了下去。

zh.text: 换句话说，堆表达力并不是校准问题的解药，有时加深加宽反而让校准更糟。真正需要的是对「认知不确定性（epistemic uncertainty）」的显式建模。这正是本文的出发点。
论文链接与代码
论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10976
代码：https://github.com/pujacomputes/gduq
项目主页：https://pujacomputes.github.io/gduq/
本文做了什么

本文有三个层层递进的贡献。第一，用一个受控案例研究证明：提升 GNN 的表达力并不能修复分布偏移下的置信度校准。第二，提出 G-∆UQ，一种把「随机中心化（stochastic centering / anchoring）」框架搬到图数据上的单模型不确定性估计方法，并且支持「部分随机化（partial stochasticity）」——只让网络的一部分变成随机的，还给出一个可以直接复用预训练模型的变体。第三，在三类分布偏移、三项安全任务上做了大规模评测。
值得强调的是「单模型」这一点：不像深度集成（Deep Ensembles）需要训练很多个模型再平均，G-∆UQ 只需要一个模型，就能给出既是预测、又是不确定性的输出。
G-∆UQ 是怎么工作的
先看方法总览。核心思路叫「锚定（anchoring）」：不再让模型直接看原始输入，而是先从训练分布里随机抽一个锚点 c，把输入改写成「相对表示」——减去锚点、再把锚点拼回来，即 [X − c ‖ c]。每次迭代换一个不同的锚点，模型就好像在从「一族假设」里采样；对同一个样本用 K 个不同锚点跑 K 次，这些预测的方差就刻画了认知不确定性。

zh.caption: 图 2　G-∆UQ 总览。作者提出三种随机中心化变体，向 GNN 注入不同程度的随机性：在节点特征上锚定（Node Feature）、在中间某个消息传递层锚定（Int. MPNN）、或在 READOUT 之后锚定（Readout）。蓝色表示随机部分、红色表示固定部分。其中 READOUT 变体只让读出后的分类头随机，因此可以直接套用预训练好的骨干网络。右侧是锚定推理（Anchored Inference）：对 K 个锚点求平均得到预测 μ，用预测的标准差 σ 度量不确定性，并给出校准后预测 μ_calib = μ(1 − σ)。

zh.text: 为什么要在特征空间、而不是在图结构上做锚定？因为如果直接对邻接矩阵做「减去锚图」，会凭空造出并不存在的边，破坏图本身的语义。所以作者选择在节点特征或隐藏表示空间里锚定。三个变体对应从早到晚不同的注入位置：越晚注入，随机的部分越少、越轻量。特别是那个「冻结预训练骨干、只训练一个带锚定的分类头」的变体，几乎是零成本地给已有模型加上了不确定性能力——这就是「部分随机化」在实践中的意义。
三类分布偏移下的表现

作者的评测刻意做得很宽。结构失真用前面的旋转 super-pixel MNIST；规模偏移（size shift）用 D&D、NCI1、NCI109、PROTEINS 四个图分类数据集，配 GCN、GIN、PNA 三种骨干；概念偏移与协变量偏移（concept / covariate shift）则用 GOOD 基准套件（GOODCMNIST-color、GOODMotif-basis、GOODMotif-size、GOODSST2-length）。对比方法包括 Vanilla、深度集成 DEns、温度缩放 Temp、蒙特卡洛 Dropout（MCD）。先看规模偏移。

zh.caption: 图 4　规模分布偏移下的预测不确定性。每组对比 G-∆UQ（蓝色）与不加锚定的基线 Base（灰色），上排为准确率（越高越好）、下排为 ECE（越低越好）。跨 D&D、NCI1、NCI109、PROTEINS 四个数据集与 GCN/GIN/PNA 三种骨干，随机中心化几乎都在降低校准误差的同时，保持甚至提升了准确率。

zh.text: 在概念与协变量偏移上，作者把与其他单模型 UQ 方法的对比放到了一起看。

zh.caption: 图 5　概念偏移与协变量偏移下的预测不确定性。横跨 GOOD 套件的四个数据集，每个数据集又分 concept 与 covariate 两种偏移；四行分别是分布内准确率（ID Acc）、分布外准确率（OOD Acc）、分布内校准（ID Cal L2）、分布外校准（OOD Cal L2）。随机中心化在保持有竞争力的分布内 / 分布外准确率的同时改善了校准，尤其是和其他单模型 UQ 方法相比时优势更明显。

zh.text: 一句话总结这三张图：不管偏移来自结构、规模还是概念 / 协变量，G-∆UQ 都能给出比其他单模型方法更可信的置信度，而准确率基本不受影响。
更可信的置信度，能换来什么
校准本身只是手段。真正的价值在于：当这些校准过的置信度被送进下游安全任务时，能不能带来更好的结果。作者考察了两项任务——泛化间隙预测和分布外检测。

zh.caption: 图 6　泛化间隙预测。用不同方法得到的置信度分数去预测泛化误差，报告平均绝对误差 MAE（越低越好），上排为分布内、下排为分布外。虽然没有哪种方法全面占优，但随机中心化非常有竞争力，在单模型 UQ 估计器里给出了数一数二低的 MAE；尤其是预训练版 G-∆UQ 表现突出，甚至超过了端到端训练的版本。

zh.text: 泛化间隙预测（在不看测试标签的情况下估计模型会掉多少点）对图来说几乎是一个尚未被探索的任务。这里预训练变体反而比端到端版本更强，是一个很实用的信号：你不必为了拿到好的不确定性而从头重训。

zh.caption: 图 7　分布外检测。报告检测 OOD 样本的 AUROC（越高越好）。在概念偏移下，G-∆UQ 的各变体与包括深度集成在内的基线都很有竞争力；在协变量偏移下，除了 GOODMotif-basis 这一个例外，预训练版 G-∆UQ 相比所有基线（包括端到端 G-∆UQ）都取得了显著提升。

zh.text: 把两项下游任务放在一起看，会发现一个反复出现的规律：预训练版 G-∆UQ 在协变量偏移这种最棘手的情形下，往往是最强的那一个。也就是说，最便宜的用法（冻结骨干、只训分类头）常常也是效果最好的用法。
一个关键的消融：锚定层选在哪

既然锚定可以放在早、中、晚三个位置，那位置到底要不要紧？作者在规模偏移最严重的 D&D 数据集上做了消融：把锚定放在 READOUT 之后（也就是最后一层），随着网络加深，准确率和校准会同时明显变好；而放在更早的层则收敛得没那么理想。由此他们给出一个实用建议——当模型预计会遇到规模偏移时，就在最后一层做随机中心化。此外，作者用神经正切核（NTK）分析确认：在中间层做常数平移是真的改变了 GNN 所表示的函数，而不是一个可被抵消的平凡重参数化。
小结与边界
本文的核心信息其实很朴素：不要指望「更大、更有表达力的图神经网络」会自动给你可信的置信度——在分布偏移下，它们不会。真正管用的做法，是把随机锚定这套原理迁移到图上。G-∆UQ 提供了一个灵活、可扩展的单模型框架，在结构、规模、概念、协变量等多种偏移、以及校准 / 泛化间隙预测 / 分布外检测三项安全任务上，都能给出可靠且校准良好的不确定性。
而它的预训练变体，让这一切几乎可以零成本地加到你已经训练好的模型上。需要留意的边界是：这些结论建立在文中特定的数据集、骨干与偏移设定之上，锚定层的最佳位置也依任务而变（例如规模偏移推荐最后一层）；把它用到新场景时，仍值得按同样的思路做一次验证。

zh.title: ICLR 2024 | 更大的图神经网络，并不会给你更可信的置信度
zh.subtitle: 密歇根大学与劳伦斯利弗莫尔国家实验室提出 G-∆UQ：一种单模型、可扩展的图神经网络认知不确定性估计方法

en.text: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly being handed high-stakes jobs: predicting molecular properties, screening materials, flagging anomalies. These settings share an uncomfortable feature: the data a model sees at test time almost never matches what it trained on. Graphs grow larger, their structure drifts, and the relationships between labels and attributes shift. In those moments we care about more than whether the model is right; we care about whether its confidence is right. Downstream safety metrics, from calibration error to out-of-distribution (OOD) rejection to generalization-gap estimation, all sit on top of that confidence indicator, which usually comes from a softmax probability or an entropy score.

The computer vision community has known for years that confidence quality decays under distribution shift. For graph neural networks, how and why confidence degrades has been studied far less. This paper (ICLR 2024) fills that gap systematically, and then offers a direct fix.

A natural first instinct is to reach for a more expressive architecture and assume better calibration comes along for free. Through a controlled experiment, the authors show it does not. Figure 1 makes the counterintuitive result hard to miss.

en.caption: Figure 1. Calibration under structural distortion shift. Models are trained on standard super-pixel MNIST and then evaluated on k-nearest-neighbor graphs built from rotated MNIST images, using the rotation angle to dial the structural distortion from mild to severe. The top row is accuracy (higher is better); the bottom row is expected calibration error, ECE (lower is better). As the shift grows, the accuracy drop is expected, but ECE deteriorates sharply too, and switching to a graph transformer (GPS), adding positional encodings (LPE), or making the network deeper and wider does not rescue it. Only the proposed G-∆UQ (blue) drives ECE down substantially without materially sacrificing accuracy.

en.text: In other words, piling on expressivity is not the cure for miscalibration, and scaling depth or width can even make it worse. What is actually needed is to model epistemic uncertainty explicitly. That is where the paper begins.

zh.caption: 图 1　结构失真分布偏移下的校准表现。作者在标准 super-pixel MNIST 上训练模型，再把它放到由「先旋转、再构图」得到的 k-近邻图上评测，用旋转角度模拟由弱到强的结构失真。上排是准确率（越高越好），下排是期望校准误差 ECE（越低越好）。随着偏移加剧，准确率下降在意料之中，但 ECE 也急剧变差——而且换成图 transformer（GPS）、加位置编码（LPE）、加深加宽网络，都救不回来。只有本文提出的 G-∆UQ（蓝色）在几乎不牺牲准确率的前提下，把 ECE 大幅压了下去。

zh.text: 本文做了什么

本文有三个层层递进的贡献。第一，用一个受控案例研究证明：提升 GNN 的表达力并不能修复分布偏移下的置信度校准。第二，提出 G-∆UQ，一种把「随机中心化（stochastic centering / anchoring）」框架搬到图数据上的单模型不确定性估计方法，并且支持「部分随机化（partial stochasticity）」——只让网络的一部分变成随机的，还给出一个可以直接复用预训练模型的变体。第三，在三类分布偏移、三项安全任务上做了大规模评测。
值得强调的是「单模型」这一点：不像深度集成（Deep Ensembles）需要训练很多个模型再平均，G-∆UQ 只需要一个模型，就能给出既是预测、又是不确定性的输出。

en.subtitle: University of Michigan and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory introduce G-∆UQ, a single-model, scalable way to estimate epistemic uncertainty in graph neural networks

zh.title: ICLR 2024 | 更大的图神经网络，并不会给你更可信的置信度
zh.subtitle: 密歇根大学与劳伦斯利弗莫尔国家实验室提出 G-∆UQ：一种单模型、可扩展的图神经网络认知不确定性估计方法

en.caption: Figure 2. Overview of G-∆UQ. The authors propose three stochastic centering variants that inject increasing-to-decreasing amounts of stochasticity into the GNN: anchoring on the node features (Node Feature), at an intermediate message-passing layer (Int. MPNN), or after the READOUT (Readout). Blue marks the stochastic part, red the static part. The READOUT variant makes only the post-readout head stochastic, so it can wrap a pretrained backbone directly. On the right is anchored inference: average over K anchors for the prediction μ, use the standard deviation σ across anchors as the uncertainty, and report the calibrated prediction μ_calib = μ(1 − σ).

en.text: What the paper contributes

The contribution comes in three escalating steps. First, a controlled case study establishing that improving a GNN's expressivity does not fix confidence calibration under distribution shift. Second, G-∆UQ, a single-model uncertainty method that ports the stochastic centering (anchoring) framework to graph data and, crucially, supports partial stochasticity (making only part of the network stochastic), including a variant that reuses a pretrained backbone as-is. Third, an extensive evaluation across three types of distribution shift and three safety-critical tasks.

The single-model point is worth dwelling on. Unlike Deep Ensembles, which train many models and average them, G-∆UQ needs just one model to produce both a prediction and an estimate of its uncertainty.
Takeaway and boundaries

The core message is plain: do not expect a larger, more expressive graph neural network to hand you trustworthy confidence: under distribution shift, it will not. The move that works is to carry the principle of stochastic anchoring over to graphs. G-∆UQ is a flexible, scalable, single-model framework that produces reliable, well-calibrated uncertainty across structural, size, concept, and covariate shifts, and across the three safety tasks of calibration, generalization-gap prediction, and OOD detection.

And its pretrained variant makes all of that nearly free to bolt onto a model you have already trained. The honest boundary: these conclusions rest on the paper's specific datasets, backbones, and shift setups, and the best anchoring layer depends on the task (last-layer is recommended for size shift). Carrying the method to a new setting still deserves the same kind of validation the authors ran here.

zh.text: 本文做了什么

本文有三个层层递进的贡献。第一，用一个受控案例研究证明：提升 GNN 的表达力并不能修复分布偏移下的置信度校准。第二，提出 G-∆UQ，一种把「随机中心化（stochastic centering / anchoring）」框架搬到图数据上的单模型不确定性估计方法，并且支持「部分随机化（partial stochasticity）」——只让网络的一部分变成随机的，还给出一个可以直接复用预训练模型的变体。第三，在三类分布偏移、三项安全任务上做了大规模评测。
值得强调的是「单模型」这一点：不像深度集成（Deep Ensembles）需要训练很多个模型再平均，G-∆UQ 只需要一个模型，就能给出既是预测、又是不确定性的输出。
G-∆UQ 是怎么工作的
先看方法总览。核心思路叫「锚定（anchoring）」：不再让模型直接看原始输入，而是先从训练分布里随机抽一个锚点 c，把输入改写成「相对表示」——减去锚点、再把锚点拼回来，即 [X − c ‖ c]。每次迭代换一个不同的锚点，模型就好像在从「一族假设」里采样；对同一个样本用 K 个不同锚点跑 K 次，这些预测的方差就刻画了认知不确定性。

zh.caption: 图 2　G-∆UQ 总览。作者提出三种随机中心化变体，向 GNN 注入不同程度的随机性：在节点特征上锚定（Node Feature）、在中间某个消息传递层锚定（Int. MPNN）、或在 READOUT 之后锚定（Readout）。蓝色表示随机部分、红色表示固定部分。其中 READOUT 变体只让读出后的分类头随机，因此可以直接套用预训练好的骨干网络。右侧是锚定推理（Anchored Inference）：对 K 个锚点求平均得到预测 μ，用预测的标准差 σ 度量不确定性，并给出校准后预测 μ_calib = μ(1 − σ)。

zh.text: 为什么要在特征空间、而不是在图结构上做锚定？因为如果直接对邻接矩阵做「减去锚图」，会凭空造出并不存在的边，破坏图本身的语义。所以作者选择在节点特征或隐藏表示空间里锚定。三个变体对应从早到晚不同的注入位置：越晚注入，随机的部分越少、越轻量。特别是那个「冻结预训练骨干、只训练一个带锚定的分类头」的变体，几乎是零成本地给已有模型加上了不确定性能力——这就是「部分随机化」在实践中的意义。

en.subtitle: University of Michigan and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory introduce G-∆UQ, a single-model, scalable way to estimate epistemic uncertainty in graph neural networks

zh.title: ICLR 2024 | 更大的图神经网络，并不会给你更可信的置信度
zh.subtitle: 密歇根大学与劳伦斯利弗莫尔国家实验室提出 G-∆UQ：一种单模型、可扩展的图神经网络认知不确定性估计方法

en.text: Results across three kinds of shift

The evaluation is deliberately broad. Structural distortion uses the rotated super-pixel MNIST benchmark from Figure 1. Size shift uses four graph-classification datasets (D&D, NCI1, NCI109, PROTEINS) with GCN, GIN, and PNA backbones. Concept and covariate shift use the GOOD benchmark suite (GOODCMNIST-color, GOODMotif-basis, GOODMotif-size, GOODSST2-length). The baselines are Vanilla, Deep Ensembles (DEns), temperature scaling (Temp), and Monte Carlo Dropout (MCD). Start with size shift.

en.caption: Figure 4. Predictive uncertainty under size distribution shift. Each pair compares G-∆UQ (blue) against a no-anchoring baseline (Base, gray), with accuracy on top (higher is better) and ECE on the bottom (lower is better). Across D&D, NCI1, NCI109, and PROTEINS and across the GCN, GIN, and PNA backbones, stochastic centering almost always lowers calibration error while maintaining or improving accuracy.

en.text: For concept and covariate shift, the authors line G-∆UQ up directly against the other single-model UQ methods.

en.caption: Figure 5. Predictive uncertainty under concept and covariate shift. Spanning the four GOOD datasets, each split into concept and covariate shift, the four rows are in-distribution accuracy (ID Acc), out-of-distribution accuracy (OOD Acc), in-distribution calibration (ID Cal L2), and out-of-distribution calibration (OOD Cal L2). Stochastic anchoring keeps ID and OOD accuracy competitive while improving calibration, and the advantage is clearest against the other single-model UQ methods.

en.text: One line summarizes all three figures: whether the shift comes from structure, size, or concept and covariate, G-∆UQ delivers more trustworthy confidence than the other single-model methods, with accuracy essentially untouched.

zh.text: 三类分布偏移下的表现

作者的评测刻意做得很宽。结构失真用前面的旋转 super-pixel MNIST；规模偏移（size shift）用 D&D、NCI1、NCI109、PROTEINS 四个图分类数据集，配 GCN、GIN、PNA 三种骨干；概念偏移与协变量偏移（concept / covariate shift）则用 GOOD 基准套件（GOODCMNIST-color、GOODMotif-basis、GOODMotif-size、GOODSST2-length）。对比方法包括 Vanilla、深度集成 DEns、温度缩放 Temp、蒙特卡洛 Dropout（MCD）。先看规模偏移。

zh.caption: 图 4　规模分布偏移下的预测不确定性。每组对比 G-∆UQ（蓝色）与不加锚定的基线 Base（灰色），上排为准确率（越高越好）、下排为 ECE（越低越好）。跨 D&D、NCI1、NCI109、PROTEINS 四个数据集与 GCN/GIN/PNA 三种骨干，随机中心化几乎都在降低校准误差的同时，保持甚至提升了准确率。

zh.text: 在概念与协变量偏移上，作者把与其他单模型 UQ 方法的对比放到了一起看。

zh.caption: 图 5　概念偏移与协变量偏移下的预测不确定性。横跨 GOOD 套件的四个数据集，每个数据集又分 concept 与 covariate 两种偏移；四行分别是分布内准确率（ID Acc）、分布外准确率（OOD Acc）、分布内校准（ID Cal L2）、分布外校准（OOD Cal L2）。随机中心化在保持有竞争力的分布内 / 分布外准确率的同时改善了校准，尤其是和其他单模型 UQ 方法相比时优势更明显。

zh.text: 一句话总结这三张图：不管偏移来自结构、规模还是概念 / 协变量，G-∆UQ 都能给出比其他单模型方法更可信的置信度，而准确率基本不受影响。

zh.title: ICLR 2024 | 更大的图神经网络，并不会给你更可信的置信度
zh.subtitle: 密歇根大学与劳伦斯利弗莫尔国家实验室提出 G-∆UQ：一种单模型、可扩展的图神经网络认知不确定性估计方法

en.text: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly being handed high-stakes jobs: predicting molecular properties, screening materials, flagging anomalies. These settings share an uncomfortable feature: the data a model sees at test time almost never matches what it trained on. Graphs grow larger, their structure drifts, and the relationships between labels and attributes shift. In those moments we care about more than whether the model is right; we care about whether its confidence is right. Downstream safety metrics, from calibration error to out-of-distribution (OOD) rejection to generalization-gap estimation, all sit on top of that confidence indicator, which usually comes from a softmax probability or an entropy score.

The computer vision community has known for years that confidence quality decays under distribution shift. For graph neural networks, how and why confidence degrades has been studied far less. This paper (ICLR 2024) fills that gap systematically, and then offers a direct fix.

A natural first instinct is to reach for a more expressive architecture and assume better calibration comes along for free. Through a controlled experiment, the authors show it does not. Figure 1 makes the counterintuitive result hard to miss.

en.caption: Figure 1. Calibration under structural distortion shift. Models are trained on standard super-pixel MNIST and then evaluated on k-nearest-neighbor graphs built from rotated MNIST images, using the rotation angle to dial the structural distortion from mild to severe. The top row is accuracy (higher is better); the bottom row is expected calibration error, ECE (lower is better). As the shift grows, the accuracy drop is expected, but ECE deteriorates sharply too, and switching to a graph transformer (GPS), adding positional encodings (LPE), or making the network deeper and wider does not rescue it. Only the proposed G-∆UQ (blue) drives ECE down substantially without materially sacrificing accuracy.

en.text: In other words, piling on expressivity is not the cure for miscalibration, and scaling depth or width can even make it worse. What is actually needed is to model epistemic uncertainty explicitly. That is where the paper begins.

zh.caption: 图 1　结构失真分布偏移下的校准表现。作者在标准 super-pixel MNIST 上训练模型，再把它放到由「先旋转、再构图」得到的 k-近邻图上评测，用旋转角度模拟由弱到强的结构失真。上排是准确率（越高越好），下排是期望校准误差 ECE（越低越好）。随着偏移加剧，准确率下降在意料之中，但 ECE 也急剧变差——而且换成图 transformer（GPS）、加位置编码（LPE）、加深加宽网络，都救不回来。只有本文提出的 G-∆UQ（蓝色）在几乎不牺牲准确率的前提下，把 ECE 大幅压了下去。

zh.text: 一个关键的消融：锚定层选在哪

既然锚定可以放在早、中、晚三个位置，那位置到底要不要紧？作者在规模偏移最严重的 D&D 数据集上做了消融：把锚定放在 READOUT 之后（也就是最后一层），随着网络加深，准确率和校准会同时明显变好；而放在更早的层则收敛得没那么理想。由此他们给出一个实用建议——当模型预计会遇到规模偏移时，就在最后一层做随机中心化。此外，作者用神经正切核（NTK）分析确认：在中间层做常数平移是真的改变了 GNN 所表示的函数，而不是一个可被抵消的平凡重参数化。

zh.text: 小结与边界
本文的核心信息其实很朴素：不要指望「更大、更有表达力的图神经网络」会自动给你可信的置信度——在分布偏移下，它们不会。真正管用的做法，是把随机锚定这套原理迁移到图上。G-∆UQ 提供了一个灵活、可扩展的单模型框架，在结构、规模、概念、协变量等多种偏移、以及校准 / 泛化间隙预测 / 分布外检测三项安全任务上，都能给出可靠且校准良好的不确定性。
而它的预训练变体，让这一切几乎可以零成本地加到你已经训练好的模型上。需要留意的边界是：这些结论建立在文中特定的数据集、骨干与偏移设定之上，锚定层的最佳位置也依任务而变（例如规模偏移推荐最后一层）；把它用到新场景时，仍值得按同样的思路做一次验证。

zh.title: ICLR 2024 | 更大的图神经网络，并不会给你更可信的置信度
zh.subtitle: 密歇根大学与劳伦斯利弗莫尔国家实验室提出 G-∆UQ：一种单模型、可扩展的图神经网络认知不确定性估计方法

en.text: How G-∆UQ works

Start with the method at a glance. The core idea is anchoring: instead of feeding the model the raw input, you first draw a random anchor c from the training distribution and rewrite the input as a relative representation: subtract the anchor, then concatenate it back, i.e. [X − c ‖ c]. Each iteration uses a different anchor, so the model behaves as if it were sampling from a family of hypotheses. Run the same sample through K different anchors, and the variance of those predictions captures epistemic uncertainty.

en.caption: Figure 2. Overview of G-∆UQ. The authors propose three stochastic centering variants that inject increasing-to-decreasing amounts of stochasticity into the GNN: anchoring on the node features (Node Feature), at an intermediate message-passing layer (Int. MPNN), or after the READOUT (Readout). Blue marks the stochastic part, red the static part. The READOUT variant makes only the post-readout head stochastic, so it can wrap a pretrained backbone directly. On the right is anchored inference: average over K anchors for the prediction μ, use the standard deviation σ across anchors as the uncertainty, and report the calibrated prediction μ_calib = μ(1 − σ).

en.text: Why anchor in feature space rather than on the graph structure itself? Subtracting an "anchor graph" from an adjacency matrix would invent edges that do not exist and corrupt the graph's meaning. So the authors anchor in node-feature or hidden-representation space instead. The three variants correspond to injecting the anchor early, in the middle, or late; the later the injection, the smaller and lighter the stochastic part. The variant that freezes a pretrained backbone and trains only an anchored classifier head adds uncertainty to an existing model at almost no cost. That is what partial stochasticity buys you in practice.
Takeaway and boundaries

The core message is plain: do not expect a larger, more expressive graph neural network to hand you trustworthy confidence: under distribution shift, it will not. The move that works is to carry the principle of stochastic anchoring over to graphs. G-∆UQ is a flexible, scalable, single-model framework that produces reliable, well-calibrated uncertainty across structural, size, concept, and covariate shifts, and across the three safety tasks of calibration, generalization-gap prediction, and OOD detection.

And its pretrained variant makes all of that nearly free to bolt onto a model you have already trained. The honest boundary: these conclusions rest on the paper's specific datasets, backbones, and shift setups, and the best anchoring layer depends on the task (last-layer is recommended for size shift). Carrying the method to a new setting still deserves the same kind of validation the authors ran here.

zh.text: 图神经网络（Graph Neural Network, GNN）正在被越来越多地放到高风险场景里：分子性质预测、材料筛选、异常检测。这些场景有一个共同点——真正的测试数据几乎不可能和训练时长得一模一样。图的规模会变、结构会变、类别与属性的关联也会变。这时候我们通常不只看模型「答得对不对」，还要看它给出的置信度（confidence indicator，通常来自 softmax 概率或熵）「可不可信」，因为校准误差、分布外（OOD）拒识、泛化间隙估计这些安全指标，全都建立在这个置信度之上。
计算机视觉领域早就知道：一旦发生分布偏移，模型的置信度质量就会明显变差。但对图神经网络来说，置信度在分布偏移下如何、以及为什么会退化，研究得要少得多。本文（ICLR 2024）系统地补上了这一课，并给出了一个直接的解决方案。
一个很自然的想法是：换更强、更有表达力的架构，校准问题是不是就能顺带解决？作者用一个受控实验给出的答案是——不能。图 1 把这个反直觉的结论摆得很清楚。

zh.caption: 图 1　结构失真分布偏移下的校准表现。作者在标准 super-pixel MNIST 上训练模型，再把它放到由「先旋转、再构图」得到的 k-近邻图上评测，用旋转角度模拟由弱到强的结构失真。上排是准确率（越高越好），下排是期望校准误差 ECE（越低越好）。随着偏移加剧，准确率下降在意料之中，但 ECE 也急剧变差——而且换成图 transformer（GPS）、加位置编码（LPE）、加深加宽网络，都救不回来。只有本文提出的 G-∆UQ（蓝色）在几乎不牺牲准确率的前提下，把 ECE 大幅压了下去。

zh.text: 换句话说，堆表达力并不是校准问题的解药，有时加深加宽反而让校准更糟。真正需要的是对「认知不确定性（epistemic uncertainty）」的显式建模。这正是本文的出发点。
三类分布偏移下的表现

作者的评测刻意做得很宽。结构失真用前面的旋转 super-pixel MNIST；规模偏移（size shift）用 D&D、NCI1、NCI109、PROTEINS 四个图分类数据集，配 GCN、GIN、PNA 三种骨干；概念偏移与协变量偏移（concept / covariate shift）则用 GOOD 基准套件（GOODCMNIST-color、GOODMotif-basis、GOODMotif-size、GOODSST2-length）。对比方法包括 Vanilla、深度集成 DEns、温度缩放 Temp、蒙特卡洛 Dropout（MCD）。先看规模偏移。

zh.caption: 图 4　规模分布偏移下的预测不确定性。每组对比 G-∆UQ（蓝色）与不加锚定的基线 Base（灰色），上排为准确率（越高越好）、下排为 ECE（越低越好）。跨 D&D、NCI1、NCI109、PROTEINS 四个数据集与 GCN/GIN/PNA 三种骨干，随机中心化几乎都在降低校准误差的同时，保持甚至提升了准确率。

zh.text: 在概念与协变量偏移上，作者把与其他单模型 UQ 方法的对比放到了一起看。

zh.caption: 图 5　概念偏移与协变量偏移下的预测不确定性。横跨 GOOD 套件的四个数据集，每个数据集又分 concept 与 covariate 两种偏移；四行分别是分布内准确率（ID Acc）、分布外准确率（OOD Acc）、分布内校准（ID Cal L2）、分布外校准（OOD Cal L2）。随机中心化在保持有竞争力的分布内 / 分布外准确率的同时改善了校准，尤其是和其他单模型 UQ 方法相比时优势更明显。

zh.text: 一句话总结这三张图：不管偏移来自结构、规模还是概念 / 协变量，G-∆UQ 都能给出比其他单模型方法更可信的置信度，而准确率基本不受影响。
